text: For Democritus and the Atomists, what is the ultimate status of the change we observe in ordinary objects (growth, decay, the burning of wood)?
choices: It is genuine change in fundamental reality, since the atoms themselves continually come to be and pass away
It is the measured cycling of an ever-living fire, governed by the Logos
It is a moving image of an eternal, changeless model, fashioned by a divine craftsman
It is only the rearrangement of permanent, unchanging atoms in the void; nothing fundamental comes to be or passes away
explanation: The Atomists explain macroscopic change as the combination and separation of eternal, indestructible atoms moving through the void - the atoms never change, only their configurations do. Option 0 contradicts the atom's defining permanence; option 1 is Heraclitus' fire-and-Logos; option 2 is Plato's moving image of eternity. Only option 3 states the atomist view.
